title: Effect Phase Order Logger
problemStatement: Implement `logLifecyclePhases()` that returns an array with the exact execution order of: `'useInsertionEffect'`, `'DOM Mutation'`, `'useLayoutEffect'`, `'Browser Paint'`, and `'useEffect'`.
interviewTrap: `useEffect` is passive and deferred until after paint. `useLayoutEffect` blocks painting.

testCases.name: useLayoutEffect runs before Browser Paint
testCases.testFn: const p = logLifecyclePhases(); return p.indexOf('useLayoutEffect') < p.indexOf('Browser Paint');

testCases.name: useEffect runs strictly after Browser Paint
testCases.testFn: const p = logLifecyclePhases(); return p.indexOf('useEffect') > p.indexOf('Browser Paint');

details.name: useEffect runs strictly after Browser Paint

detailedExplanation.conceptualOverview: React provides three distinct effect hooks that run at different stages of the commit phase: `useInsertionEffect` (runs first, synchronously before DOM mutations for CSS-in-JS libraries), `useLayoutEffect` (runs second, synchronously after DOM mutations before browser paint), and `useEffect` (runs third, asynchronously after browser paint).
stepByStepWalkthrough: Construct an Effect Phase Order Logger that executes simulated components.
Log each lifecycle step: Render -> Insertion Effects -> DOM Mutated -> Layout Effects -> Browser Paint -> Passive Effects.
Demonstrate that `useInsertionEffect` executes first, then `useLayoutEffect`, and finally `useEffect` asynchronously.
Verify cleanup execution order during unmounts and updates.
detailedExplanation.underlyingEngineInternals: In `ReactFiberCommitWork.js`, `commitMutationEffects` mutates the DOM. Immediately prior, `commitInsertionEffectOnFiber` fires `useInsertionEffect`. Immediately following, `commitLayoutEffects` fires `useLayoutEffect`. Then control yields to the browser paint engine. After paint, `flushPassiveEffects` drains `useEffect` queues.

complexity.time: O(E) where E is total count of effects across components.

edgeCasesHandled: Strict lifecycle sequence verification across all 3 hook types.
Effect cleanups run prior to re-execution in corresponding phases.
Passive effects defer execution until after paint.

specifications: React Official Docs: Synchronizing with Effects vs Layout Effects vs Insertion Effects
verifiedRules: useInsertionEffect runs synchronously before DOM mutations.
useLayoutEffect runs synchronously after DOM mutations and blocks paint.
useEffect runs asynchronously after browser paint.

interviewCrossQuestions.question: What is the exact execution order of useInsertionEffect, useLayoutEffect, and useEffect?
interviewCrossQuestions.answer: 1) Component renders. 2) `useInsertionEffect` cleanups and callbacks run synchronously before DOM mutations (for CSS-in-JS). 3) Host DOM mutations occur. 4) `useLayoutEffect` cleanups and callbacks run synchronously after DOM mutations, before browser paint. 5) Browser paints the screen. 6) `useEffect` cleanups and callbacks run asynchronously after paint.
interviewCrossQuestions.whyAsked: The universal test for React effect lifecycle timing.

interviewCrossQuestions.question: Why was useInsertionEffect introduced in React 18?
interviewCrossQuestions.answer: CSS-in-JS libraries (Emotion, Styled-Components) injecting `<style>` tags during `useLayoutEffect` forced the browser to recalculate CSS styles and layouts multiple times before paint. `useInsertionEffect` runs before DOM mutations, allowing styles to be injected into `<head>` before any layout measurements occur.
interviewCrossQuestions.whyAsked: Tests understanding of CSS-in-JS runtime engine integration.

realWorldUseCases.description: Emotion and Styled-Components injecting runtime CSS classes before elements mount.

howToExplain.opening: React provides three effect hooks targeting different stages of the commit pipeline: Insertion (pre-DOM), Layout (post-DOM pre-paint), and Passive (post-paint).
keyPoints: useInsertionEffect runs before DOM mutations for CSS-in-JS.
useLayoutEffect runs after DOM mutations before browser paint.
useEffect runs asynchronously after browser paint.
Always default to useEffect unless synchronous DOM measurement is required.
howToExplain.closingImpression: Selecting the correct effect hook prevents layout thrashing, style recalculations, and dropped animation frames.
analogies: Stage lighting: useInsertionEffect sets up light bulbs; useLayoutEffect adjusts spotlights while the curtain is down; useEffect starts playing background music after the curtain rises.

commonMistakes.why: useLayoutEffect blocks browser paint; fetching data here freezes the screen.
commonMistakes.correct: Use useEffect for all non-visual operations.

followUpDeepDive.question: Why does useLayoutEffect log a warning during Server-Side Rendering (SSR)?
followUpDeepDive.answer: Because on the server there is no DOM and no paint! `useLayoutEffect` cannot execute on the server, producing a mismatch between client and server renders.
